sanskrit_sloka:
మాం హి పార్థ వ్యపాశ్రిత్య యేఽపి స్యుః  పాపయోనయః ।
స్త్రియో వైశ్యాస్తథాశూద్రాః తేఽ పి యాంతి పరాం గతిమ్  ।। 32 ।।
translation_english: Regardless of their birth, race, caste, gender, or even the society's abominations, all those who take refuge in Me attain the Supreme Word.
explanation_english:
Jivas (Jivatmas) who are fortunate enough to be born in pious families, are trained in good values ​​and pious living right from childhood. It is the meritorious fruit of their previous births. At the same time, some other beings - drunkards, criminals, drug addicts and atheists are unfortunate to be born in families. This, too, is the result of sins in their previous births.

Regardless of their birth, sex, or caste, if one takes complete refuge in God, they will attain the supreme goal. By this we can understand the greatness of the path of devotion which is accessible to all. But, other routes have very strict rules for eligibility.

As for the qualification of Jnana Yoga, Jagadguru Shankaracharya states:

Vivekino Viraktasya Samadiguna Shalinahmumukshoraiva hi Brahma Jignasa Yogyata Mata

"Discretion, dispassion, controlled mind-senses and intense longing for salvation - only those who possess these four qualities - are eligible to adopt the path of Jnana Yoga."

In the path of Karma Kanda (Vedic rituals), six precepts are to be observed.

Dese kala upayena dravyaam sraddha samanvithampatre pradiyate yattat sakalam dharma sakham

"Six conditions must be fulfilled for the performance of the ritualistic rites - right place, right time, right method and flawless chanting of the mantra, purity of the material used, a qualified Brahmin to perform the yajna, and complete faith in the ritual - all these must be present."

Even in the Ashtanga yoga path, there are strict rules:

Suchau dese pratishtapya (Bhagavatam 3.28.8)

"Sit still in proper asana and do hatha yoga in a sacred place."

Compared to all this, bhakti yoga is so easy that it can be done by anyone, at any time, in any place, in any condition, with any material.

Na Desha Niyamastasmin Na Kala Niyamasthatha (Padma Purana)

What this sloka says is that God is not related to time and place when we worship him with devotion. He sees only the love in our heart. All souls (living beings) are children of God. He is willing to welcome all who come to Him with open arms.
word_by_word_meaning_english: mam — my own; hi — truly; Partha — Arjuna, son of Pritha; vyapasritya — taking refuge (refuge); ye — whoever; api — even so; syuh — even so; papa yonayah — low birth; striyah — women; vaishyah — the Vaishyas; tatha — and; sudrah — workers; te api — even they; yanti — do not go; param — supreme (supreme); Path — destination.

sanskrit_sloka:
కిం పునర్బ్రాహ్మణాః  పుణ్యా భక్తా రాజర్షయస్తథా ।
అనిత్యమసుఖం లోకమిమం  ప్రాప్య  భజస్వ మామ్ ।। 33 ।।
translation_english: And what to say about the pious kings and ancestors? So, after entering this temporary and pleasureless world, engage in me with devotion.
explanation_english: When even the most abominable sinners are guaranteed to succeed in the path of devotion, why should the higher souls still doubt? Kings and Munas, should have even more absolute faith that through the path of Ananya Bhakti the Supreme Word can be attained.  Shri Krishna suggests, "A pious king like you should be steadfast in the knowledge that this world is impermanent and abode of sorrows. Be engaged in devotion to Me, the form of infinite eternal bliss. Otherwise, birth in the family of saints and kings, good education and favorable material conditions, we cannot use in the pursuit of the highest goal. will be wasted."
word_by_word_meaning_english: Kim — What? re — then; brahminah — the gods; punyah — pious souls; bhakta — devotees; raja-rishaya — the great kings; tatha — and; anityam — temporary; asukham — without pleasure; loka — the world; imam — of this; prapya — after obtaining; bhajasva — engage in devotion; Mam — in me.

sanskrit_sloka:
మన్మనా భవ మద్భక్తో మద్యాజీ మాం నమస్కురు ।
మామేవైష్యసి యుక్త్వైవమ్ ఆత్మానం మత్పరాయణః ।। 34 ।।
translation_english: Always remember Me, be devoted to Me, worship Me and offer obeisances to Me. Undoubtedly you will come to Me when your mind and body are offered to Me.
explanation_english:
Throughout this chapter, Pidapa, having spoken of the greatness of the path of devotion, Sri Krishna now concludes this chapter by praying Arjuna to become his devotee. He tells Arjuna to unite his mind with the Lord in true yoga by worshiping him, by meditating with his mind on his divine Mars form, by bowing to him with pure humility.

'Namaskuru' (bowing down with humility) neutralizes any egoistic qualities in devotional practice. In this way, without pride, the heart is immersed in devotion and all our thoughts and activities should be submitted to God.  Sri Krishna assures Arjuna that this kind of bhakti yogic unity will surely lead to the attainment of Bhagavat; There should be no doubt about it.
word_by_word_meaning_english: mat-manah — always remember Me; bhava — be; mat — of me; bhaktah — devotee; Mat yaji — You do not worship me; mam namaskuru — salute me; Mam eva — I am sure; asyasi — will reach; yuktva — united with me; evam — in this way; atmanam — your mind and body; Mat-parayana — being devoted to Me.

sanskrit_sloka:
శ్రీ భగవానువాచ ।
భూయ ఏవ మహాబాహో శృణు మే పరమం వచః  ।
యత్తేఽహం ప్రీయమాణాయ వక్ష్యామి హితకామ్యయా ।। 1 ।।
translation_english: Sri Bhagavan spoke thus: Hear again my divine instruction, O great-armed one. Since you are my beloved friend, I will inform you of them for your pleasure.
explanation_english: Lord Krishna was pleased to see Arjuna's keen interest in hearing his glories. Now, to increase his happiness and to inflame his enthusiasm for loving devotion, says Sri Krishna, I will declare His wonderful glories and unique qualities. He uses the words "Priyamanaya", which means, "You are my beloved friend, therefore I am imparting this most special knowledge to you."
word_by_word_meaning_english: Sri Bhagavanuvacha — Lord Palikenu; bhuyah — again; eva — truly; maha-baho — of the great arms; srinu — hear; May — of me ; param — divine; vacah — instruction; yat — whatever; te — to you; Aham — I; Priyamanaya — You are my dear friend; vaksyami — I will tell; hitakamaya — seeking your good.

sanskrit_sloka:
న మే విదుః సురగణాః ప్రభవం న మహర్షయః ।
అహమాదిర్హి దేవానాం మహర్షీణాం చ సర్వశః ।। 2 ।।
translation_english: Neither the gods nor the sages know my place of origin. I am the source of origin for devas and sages.
explanation_english:
A father knows the birth and life of his sons because he sees it firsthand. But, his father's birth and childhood were unknown to his sons because they happened before their birth. Similarly, demigods and rishis cannot understand the real nature of God's original position because God exists before their birth. Therefore, the Rigveda states:

Ko addha veda ka iha pravochat, kuta a jata kuta iyam visrishtihaarvag deva asya visaranaya, atha ko veda yata ababhuva (10.129.6)

"Who in this world has clarity? Who can say where this universe was born? Who can say where this creation came from? Gods came after creation. So, who knows where this universe originated from?"

Nainaddeva Apnuvan Purvamarshat (Ishopanishad 4)

"God is not unknown to the gods, for He has existed before them." However, to increase the devotion of his beloved, such esoteric knowledge is now being imparted by Lord Krishna.
word_by_word_meaning_english: na — not; May — of me; viduh — knows; sura-ganah — the deities; prabhavam — origin; na — not; maha-rishayah — sages; Aham — I; adih — the original source; hi — truly; devanam — of the gods; maha-risinam — of the sages; Cha — and; sarvasah—in all kinds of ways.

sanskrit_sloka:
యో మామజమనాదిం చ వేత్తి లోకమహేశ్వరమ్ ।
అసమ్మూఢః స మర్త్యేషు సర్వపాపైః ప్రముచ్యతే ।। 3 ।।
translation_english: Knowing that I am birthless and without adi(beginnings) and that I am the Maheshvara of all the worlds, men do not fall into delusion and they are freed from all sins.
explanation_english:
Pidapa who said that no one can know him, Sri Krishna now says that some people know him. Is he contradicting himself? No, he means that no one can know God by his own effort, but if God Himself graces anyone, that fortunate soul can know Him. Therefore, all those who have been able to know God have been able to do so only by His divine grace. As Krishna says in the 10th verse of this chapter: "To those whose minds are devoted to Me, I bestow My divine knowledge; thereby they attain Me effortlessly." Here, those who know that Sri Krishna is the Supreme Lord are no longer under illusion. Such fortunate souls are released from their past and present karmic bonds and develop loving devotion towards Him.

To convey the difference between the living entities and Himself, Sri Krishna declares that He is the Lord of all the worlds. The same thing is said in the Swetasvatara Upanishad:

Tamishvaranam Param Mahesvarantam Devatanam Param Cha Deivatampatim Patinam Param Parastadvidama Devam Bhuvanesamedyam (6.7)

"The Lord is the God of all the Gods; He is the God of all the Gods. He is the Beloved of all the Beloved; He is the Ruler of this world, and is beyond the power of material nature."
word_by_word_meaning_english: yah — whoever; Mom — me; ajam — birthless; anadim — beginningless; Cha — and; vetti — know; loka — of this world; maha-esvaram — of Mahesvara; asammudha — one who is not delusional; sah — they; martyesu — among human beings; sarva-papaih — from all sins; pramuchyate — will be liberated.

sanskrit_sloka:
బుద్ధిః  జ్ఞానమసమ్మోహః క్షమా సత్యం దమః శమః  ।
సుఖం దుఃఖం భవోఽభావో భయం చాభయమేవ చ ।। 4 ।।

అహింసా సమతా తుష్టిస్తపో  దానం యశోఽయశః ।
భవంతి భావా భూతానాం మత్త ఏవ పృథగ్విధాః  ।। 5 ।।
translation_english: Intelligence, knowledge, clarity of thought, kindness, honesty, restraint of mind and senses, pleasures and sorrows, births and deaths, fear and courage, non-violence, equanimity, contentment, austerity, charity, fame and infamy, etc. - the variety of qualities that exist in human beings are born from the various Me.
explanation_english:
In these two slokas, Sri Krishna continues to prove his philosophy of Parameshwara and his absolute supremacy over the entire creation. Here, he mentions twenty types of feelings/characteristics found in different parts of each human being. He declares that all the various feelings, emotions and dispositions that arise in the human race come from Himself.

Buddhi is the ability to analyze things in the right perspective.

Jnana is the ability to distinguish between what is spiritual and what is material.

Disillusionment means lack of confusion/disillusionment.

Forgiveness is the ability to forgive those who have harmed us.

Satyam means boldly proclaiming the truth for the welfare of all people.

Dama means to restrain the senses from their objects.

Shama means controlling and restraining the mind.

Sukham is the feeling of joy and happiness.

Grief is a feeling of hardship and anguish.

Bhava means 'I am'.

Abhavah means the experience of death.

Fear is the fear of impending trouble.

Abhaya means freedom from fear.

Ahimsa means not to harm any living being by mind, word or action.

Samata means to remain one even in favorable or unfavorable circumstances.

Tushti means being satisfied with whatever one gets as a result of karma.

Tapa is voluntary devotion for spiritual purpose as prescribed by the Vedas.

Danam means charity given to those who are deserving.

Yasamu means fame due to good qualities.

Ayasha is the infamy caused by bad qualities.

Lord Krishna states that these qualities manifest in people as much as He allows. Therefore, He is the source of the good and bad nature of all living beings. It is like the electric power supplied by the power plant is used by various appliances. The same electrical energy can produce different results when passed through different devices. One produces sound, another produces light, and the third produces heat. Although expressed in different ways, their source is the same, the electric power given from the same power station. Similarly, depending on the purusartha (actions done using our free will) of our previous and present births, the energy given by the Lord manifests in us as good or bad.
word_by_word_meaning_english: buddhih — intelligence;  jnana — knowledge; asammohah — clarity of thought; kshama — quality of forgiveness; satyam — truthfulness; damah — sense restraint; shamah — control of the mind; sukham — pleasure; duhkham — sorrow; bhavah — birth; abhavah — death; bhaya — fear; Cha — and; abhaya — courage; eva — truly; Cha — and; ahimsa — non-violence; samatha — equality;  tushtih — satisfaction; tapah — penance; dana — donation; yasah — glory; ayasah — defamation; bhavanti — born; bhavah — feelings/qualities; Bhutan — among men; mattah — from me; eva — only; prthak-vidhah — of different kinds.

sanskrit_sloka:
మహర్షయః సప్త పూర్వే చత్వారో మనవస్తథా ।
మద్భావా మానసా జాతా యేషాం లోక ఇమాః ప్రజాః ।। 6 ।।
translation_english: The seven sages, the four Mahatmas before them, the fourteen Manus – all these were born from my mind. All the people of this world have descended from them.
explanation_english:
Here Sri Krishna continues to say how he is the source of all the material and poisons in the universe; Earlier he mentioned twenty qualities; Now he mentions twenty-five great Mahatmas. These are the seven Rishis, the four Supreme Mahatmas; Fourteen Manus. He also summarizes the genealogy of the entire universe from Himself.

Lord Brahma was born from the Hiranyagarbha Shakti of Vishnu Murthy (the form of God responsible for the maintenance of the material world). Four great souls were born from Brahma – Vare, Sanak, Sanandan, Sanat and Sanatan. These are called four sons. In our universe, these four sons are the children of Lord Brahma before all others. Since they are born (in an asexual manner) from the mind of Lord Brahma, they have no mother. As they are eternally liberated souls and adepts in Yoga Shastra, they are empowered to help others attain salvation through spiritual practice. After Kumararishis came Sapta Rishis. These are Maricha, Angira, Atri, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu and Vasistha. They were given the task of increasing the human population. After that came the fourteen Manus, Swayambhuva, Svarochisha, Uttam, Tamasa, Raivata, Chakshusha, Vaivasvata, Savarni, Dakshasavarni, Brahmasavarni, Dharmasavarni, Rudra-putra, Rochya and Bhavutyaka. They were given the authority to administer the race of Manasya from the time of the gods and uphold the Vedic dharma. We are currently in the period of Vaivasvata Manu, the seventh Manu. This period is therefore called Vaivasvata Manvantara. In this present Kalpa (day of Lord Brahma) there will be seven more Manus.

Deva worlds have many deities to manage the universe. All these are the sons and grandsons of Brahma; Lord Brahma was born from Vishnu Murthy, Vishnu Murthy is also the incarnation of Sri Krishna. Therefore, it can be said that Sri Krishna is the root man (prapitamah) of all the root men.
word_by_word_meaning_english: maha-rishaya — sages; sapta — seven; purve — before that; chatvarah — four; manavah — the manuvas; tatha— and; mat bhavah — emanating from Me; manasah — mind; jatah — were born; yesham — from them; loke — in the world; imah — all of them; prajah — the people.

sanskrit_sloka:
ఏతాం విభూతిం యోగం చ మమ యో వేత్తి తత్త్వతః ।
సోఽవికంపేన యోగేన యుజ్యతే నాత్ర సంశయః ।। 7 ।।
translation_english: Those who truly know My glories (vibhutas) and divine powers become one with Me through the yoga of unceasing devotion. There is no doubt about this.
explanation_english:
The word Vibhuti refers to the great power of God manifested in the universe. The word yoga refers to God's relationship with these wonderful energies. Sri Krishna says in this sloka that whenever we become aware of the wonderful glories of the Supreme Lord, and when we have faith in His glories, we naturally engage in His devotion.

Knowledge of God's glories increases the love of the devotees and sharpens their devotion. Knowledge and love have a direct connection as illustrated in this next example. Suppose your friend shows you something like a black pebble. You have no understanding of its goodness and hence no love for it. Your friend says, "This is a Saligrama, a Mahatma gifted it to me". A Saligrama is a special rock that is worshiped as a form of Lord Vishnu. When you know the significance of the Saligrama, when you know that the stone is a Saligrama, your respect for it increases. If your friend says something else like this, "Did you know that it was worshiped five hundred years ago by a great Mahatma, Swami Ramananda?" The moment you hear this, your respect for the stone will increase. Every time, knowledge of this stone increases respect for it. Similarly, proper understanding/knowledge of God leads to devotion towards Him. Thus, the Pidapa, Shri Krishna, who has elaborated the glorious glory of the Lord manifesting in the workings of the infinite Brahmanas, means that whoever is established in this knowledge becomes one with Him with unwavering devotion.
word_by_word_meaning_english: etham — this; vibhutim — glories; yoga — divine powers; Cha — and; mama — of me; yah — whoever; vetti — knowing; tattvatah — truly; sah — they; avikalpena — unwavering; yogena — in the yoga of bhakti; yujyate — become one; na —no; atra — here; samsayah — doubt.

sanskrit_sloka:
అహం సర్వస్య ప్రభవో మత్తః సర్వం ప్రవర్తతే ।
ఇతి మత్వా భజంతే మాం బుధా భావసమన్వితాః ।। 8 ।।
translation_english: I am the source of all creation. Everything is going on because of me. Knowing this fully, the sages worship Me with the utmost devotion and faith.
explanation_english:
శ్రీ కృష్ణుడు ఈ శ్లోకాన్ని "అహం సర్వస్య ప్రభవో" అనటంతో ప్రారంభిస్తున్నాడు, అంటే "నేనే సర్వోత్కృష్ట పరమ సత్యమును మరియు సర్వ కారణ కారణమును" అని. ఈ విషయాన్ని 7.7, 7.12, 10.5 మరియు 15.15వ శ్లోకాలలో, భగవద్గీత లో చాలా సార్లు చెప్పాడు. ఇతర పురాణ/ఇతిహాసాలలో కూడా ఇది గట్టిగా పేర్కొనబడినది. ఋగ్వేదము ప్రకారం:

యం కామయే తం తం ఉగ్రం కృష్ణోమి తం బ్రహ్మాణం తమ్ ఋషిం తం సుమేద్సం (10.125.5)

"నేను ప్రేమించే వారిని అత్యంత మహానీయులుగా చేస్తాను; వారిని పురుషులుగా లేదా స్త్రీలగా చేస్తాను; వారిని జ్ఞానవంతులైన మహాత్ములుగా చేస్తాను; ఏదేని జీవాత్మను బ్రహ్మ పదవికి అర్హునిగా చేస్తాను." ఈ నిజాన్ని అర్థం చేసుకున్న వివేకులు ధృడ విశ్వాసం పెంచుకుని మరియు ప్రేమయుక్త భక్తితో ఆయనను ఆరాధిస్తారు.

ఈ విధంగా శ్రీ కృష్ణుడు ఈ భౌతిక జగత్తుకి మరియు ఆధ్యాత్మిక జగత్తుకి, రెండింటికీ కూడా సర్వేశ్వరుడు. కానీ, కేవలం ఈ సృష్టి నిర్వహణయే భగవంతుని యొక్క ప్రధానమైన కార్యము కాదు. చైతన్య మహాప్రభు ఇలా పేర్కొన్నాడు:

స్వయం భగవానేర కర్మ నహే భార-హరణ (చైతన్య చరితామృతము, ఆది లీల 4.8)

"శ్రీ కృష్ణుడు తానే స్వయంగా ఈ భౌతిక విశ్వముల యొక్క సృష్టి, స్థితి మరియు లయములో నిమగ్నం కాడు." శ్రీ కృష్ణుడి ప్రధాన కార్యము ఏమిటంటే, ముక్తి/మోక్షము సాధించిన జీవులతో తన దివ్య ధామము గోలోకములో ప్రేమ యుక్త నిత్య లీలలలో నిమగ్నమవ్వటమే. భౌతిక సృష్టి నిమిత్తం, ఆయనే కారణోదక్షాయి విష్ణు స్వరూపంగా అవతరిస్తాడు, ఆయననే మహావిష్ణువు అని కూడా అంటారు.

ఈ విధంగా, అనంతమైన భౌతిక విశ్వములను కలిగి ఉన్న ఈ భౌతిక సృష్టిపై ఆధిపత్యానికి ఉన్న భగవంతుని స్వరూపమే మహావిష్ణువు. మహా విష్ణువునే ప్రథమ పురుషుడు అని కూడా అంటారు (భౌతిక జగత్తులో భగవంతుని యొక్క ప్రథమ స్వరూపము). ఆయన కారణ సముద్రంలో దివ్య నీటిలో ఉంటూ అనంతమైన బ్రహ్మాండాలను తన శరీర రోమ కూపాల్లోంచి సృజిస్తూ ఉంటాడు. తదుపరి ఆయనే ప్రతి ఒక్క బ్రహ్మాండం క్రింద గర్భోదక్షాయి విష్ణు స్వరూపంలో వ్యాప్తించి ఉంటాడు, ఆయననే ద్వితీయ పురుషుడు అంటారు. (భౌతిక ప్రపంచంలో రెండవ స్వరూపము).

గర్భోదక్షాయి విష్ణు నుండి బ్రహ్మ జన్మించాడు. ఆయనే సృష్టి క్రమాన్ని నిర్దేశిస్తాడు – విశ్వము యొక్క విభిన్నములైన స్థూల, సూక్ష్మ పదార్ధాలని, ప్రకృతి నియమాలని, గ్రహాలూ, పాలపుంతలూ, వాటిపై నివసించే జీవరాశులు మొదలైన వన్నీటినీ సృష్టిస్తూ ఉంటాడు. కాబట్టి బ్రహ్మని విశ్వ సృష్టి కర్త అని అంటూ ఉంటారు, నిజానికి ఆయన ద్వితీయ స్థాన సృష్టికర్త.

గర్భోదకశాయి విష్ణు ఇంకొంత వ్యాప్తి నొంది, తానే, క్షీరోదక్షాయి విష్ణు గా రూపాంతరం చెంది, ప్రతి బ్రహ్మాండం యొక్క పై భాగంలో, క్షీర సాగరంలో నివసిస్తాడు. క్షీరోదక్షాయి విష్ణువు నే తృతీయ పురుషుడు అంటారు. (భౌతిక జగత్తు లో భగవంతుని యొక్క మూడవ రూపాంతరము). విశ్వం పైన ఉంటాడు కానీ తానే పరమాత్మ రూపంలో సర్వ ప్రాణుల హృదయములో, వాటి కర్మలను గమనిస్తూ, వాటి లెక్క గణిస్తూ, సరైన సమయంలో కర్మ ఫలాలని అందచేస్తూ ఉంటాడు. అందుకే ఆయనను విశ్వ స్థితికారకుడు అంటారు.

ఇక్కడ చెప్పబడిన విష్ణు మూర్తి స్వరూపాలన్నీ శ్రీ కృష్ణుడి కన్నా అబేధములే. అందుకే, ఈ శ్లోకంలో సమస్త ఆధ్యాత్మిక మరియు భౌతిక సృష్టి ఆయన నుండే వచ్చాయి అని అంటున్నాడు. శ్రీ కృష్ణుడు నే ‘అవతారీ’ (అన్ని అవతారముల మూలము) అని కూడా అంటారు. శ్రీమద్ భాగవతము ప్రకారం : ఏతే చాంశ కలాః పుంసః కృష్ణస్తు భగవాన్ స్వయం (1.3.28) “భగవంతుని సమస్త స్వరూపాలు శ్రీ కృష్ణుడి రూపాంతరాలే లేదా ఆయన రూపాంతరాల రూపాంతరాలే; ఆయన మాత్రం స్వయం భగవానుడు. అందుకే, ద్వితీయ స్థాన సృష్టికర్త అయిన బ్రహ్మ, శ్రీ కృష్ణుడిని ఈ విధంగా స్తుతించాడు:

యస్యైకనిశ్వసిత కాలమథావలంబ్యజీవంతి లోమవిలజా జగదండనాథాఃవిష్ణుర్మహాన్ సఇహయస్య కలావిషేశోగోవిందమాది పురుషం తమహం భజామి (బ్రహ్మ సంహిత 5.48)

“అనంతమైన బ్రహ్మాండాలు – ప్రతి ఒక్క దాంట్లో ఒక శంకరుడు, బ్రహ్మ, మరియు విష్ణు ఉన్నటువంటివి – శ్రీ మహా విష్ణువు శరీర రోమ కూపాల్లోంచి ఆయన శ్వాస తీసుకున్నప్పుడు సృజించబడుతాయి; మరియు ఆయన శ్వాస విడిచినప్పుడు ఆయనలోకే లయమై పోతాయి. అటువంటి శ్రీ మహా విష్ణువు మూల స్వరూపమైన శ్రీ కృష్ణుడిని నేను పూజిస్తాను.” శ్రీ కృష్ణుడు ఇక ఇప్పుడు భక్తులు తనను ఎలా భజిస్తారో వివరిస్తున్నాడు.
word_by_word_meaning_english: Aham — I; sarvasya — of the entire creation; prabhavah — the place of original production; mattah — from myself; sarvam — all things; pravartate — pravartillunu (to walk); iti — in this way; matwa — knowing; bhajante — worshiped; mam — me; budhah — the wise; bhava-samanvitah — with utmost faith and devotion.

sanskrit_sloka:
మచ్చిత్తా మద్గతప్రాణా బోధయంతః పరస్పరమ్ ।
కథయంతశ్చ మాం నిత్యం తుష్యంతి చ రమంతి చ ।। 9 ।।
translation_english: My devotees are always satisfied with Me when their minds ascend to Me and their lives are surrendered to Me. Telling each other about Me and discussing My glories, they experience the greatest satisfaction and bliss.
explanation_english:
మనస్సు యొక్క స్వభావమేమిటంటే దానికిష్టమైన దానిపై అది లగ్నమై పోతుంది. ఆయన యందు గాఢమైన అభిమానం పెంచుకోవటం వలన భగవంతుని భక్తులు ఆయనను గుర్తుచేసుకుంటూ స్మరించటంలో నిమగ్నమై పోతారు. ఆయన పట్ల భక్తియే వారి జీవితానికి ఆధారంగా ఉంటుంది, దాని నుండే వారి జీవిత పరమార్ధం, లక్ష్యం, బ్రతుకేందుకు శక్తిని పొందుతారు. ఒక చేపకు నీరు ఎలా అవసరమో వారికి భగవత్ స్మరణ అలా అవసరము అని భావిస్తారు.

వ్యక్తుల హృదయానికి ఏది ఇష్టమైనదో తెలుసుకోవాలంటే వారు తమ మనస్సు, శరీరము మరియు సంపదను దేనికి అంకితం చేస్తారో దాని బట్టి తెలుసుకోవచ్చు. బైబిల్ ఇలా పేర్కొంటుంది: For where your treasure is, there your heart will also be.” (Matthew 6:21).  వ్యక్తుల మనస్సు ఎక్కడ ఉందో తెలుసుకోవాలంటే వారి చెక్కుపుస్తకం మరియు క్రెడిట్ కార్డు లావాదేవీలు చూస్తే సరిపోతుంది. ఒకవేళ వారు ఖరీదైన వాహనాల కోసం డబ్బు ఖర్చు పెడుతుంటే వారి మనస్సు వాటిపై ఉన్నట్టు. ఒకవేళ వారు విలాసవంతమైన సెలవులపై బాగా ఖర్చు పెడుతుంటే, అదే వారికి బాగా నచ్చే విషయమన్నట్టు.  ఒకవేళ వారు ఆఫ్రికా లో ఎయిడ్స్ జబ్బుతో ఉన్న పిల్లలకై విరాళం దానం చేస్తుంటే, ఆ విషయమే వారి యొక్క మనస్సులో ఉన్నట్టు. తల్లిదండ్రులకు వారి పిల్లల పట్ల ప్రేమ అనేది, వారి పట్ల సమయము, డబ్బు వెచ్చించే వైనంతో మనకు తెలుస్తుంది. ఇదే విధంగా, భక్తుల యొక్క ప్రేమ అనేది వారి భగవంతునికే అంకితమయ్యే తీరుతో ప్రకటితమవుతుంది. శ్రీ కృష్ణుడు మద్-గత-ప్రాణాః, అంటే, ‘నా భక్తులు వారి జీవితాన్ని నాకే అంకితం చేస్తారు’ అని అర్థం.

ఇటువంటి శరణాగతి నుండి తృప్తి లభిస్తుంది. భక్తులు తమ కార్యకలాపముల ఫలితాన్ని వారికి ఇష్టమైన భగవంతునికే సమర్పిస్తారు కాబట్టి, వారు ప్రతి సందర్భము/పరిస్థితి ఆయన నుండే వస్తున్నది అని భావిస్తారు. కాబట్టి, వారు అనుకూల మరియు ప్రతికూల పరిస్థితులను కూడా భగవత్ సంకల్పము గా చూస్తారు, మరియు ఈ రెంటిలో కూడా సమత్వ బుద్ధితో ఉంటారు.

భగవంతుని పై భక్తుల యొక్క ప్రేమ, పైన పేర్కొన్న రూపాలలో వ్యక్తమయినా, అది వారి పెదవులపై కూడా ప్రకటితమవుతుంది. వారికి భగవంతుని వైభవము, ఆయన నామములు, రూపములు, గుణములు, లీలలు, ధామములు మరియు భక్తుల గురించి మాట్లాడుకోవటం అత్యంత ఆనందదాయకంగా ఉంటుంది.  ఈ ప్రకారంగా భగవంతుని వైభవాల,  కీర్తన మరియు శ్రవణ ప్రక్రియలలో వారు ఆనందం అనుభవించటమే కాక, దానిని ఇతరులతో కూడా పంచుకుంటారు. తమలో తమ ఆధ్యాత్మిక పురోగతి కోసం, భగవంతుని దివ్య జ్ఞానాన్ని ఇతరులతో పంచుకుంటూ,  ఒకరికి ఒకరు సహకరించుకుంటారు (బోధయంతి). భగవంతుని లీలలు, వైభవము గురించి మాట్లాటడం మరియు పాడటం భక్తులకు పరమ సంతృప్తిని (తుశ్యంతి) మరియు ఆనందాన్ని (రమంతి) కలుగ చేస్తుంది. ఈ విధంగా తలచుకోవటం, వినటం మరియు జపించే ప్రక్రియల ద్వారా వారు భగవంతుడిని ఆరాధిస్తుంటారు.  ఇదే త్రివిధా భక్తి అంటే - శ్రవణం కీర్తనం, మరియు స్మరణం.  9.14వ శ్లోక వ్యాఖ్యానం లో ఇది ఇంతకు క్రితం వివరించబడినది.

తన భక్తులు తనను ఎలా ఆరాధిస్తారో చెప్పిన పిదప, శ్రీ కృష్ణుడు, తను, వారి భక్తి కి ఎలా ప్రతిస్పందిస్తాడో ఇప్పుడిక చెప్తాడు.
word_by_word_meaning_english: mat-chittah — my mind ascended; mat-gata-pranah — having surrendered to Me; bodhayantah — instructing (with the divine knowledge of the Lord); mutual — to each other; kathayantah — tell; Cha — and; mam — about me; nityam — eternally; tusyanti — satisfaction; Cha — and; ramanti — (they) rejoice; Cha — and.

sanskrit_sloka:
తేషాం సతతయుక్తానాం భజతాం ప్రీతిపూర్వకమ్ ।
దదామి బుద్ధియోగం తం యేన మాముపయాంతి తే ।। 10 ।।
translation_english: To those whose mind is united with Me in loving devotion, I bestow divine knowledge by which they may attain Me.
explanation_english:
We cannot receive the divine knowledge of God by our own intelligence. No matter how intelligent we are, we have to admit that ultimately our intellect is made up of physical forces. Therefore, our thoughts, wisdom, and wisdom are limited to the material mundane world. God and His divine world are beyond our physical intellect. The Vedas have strongly emphasized this point.

Yasya religion Tasya religion Religion Yasya na Veda sahavijnatam vijanatam vijnatamavijanatam (Kenopanishat 2.3)

"Those who think that they know God by their intellect have no understanding of God. Only those who know that God is beyond the limits of their intellect have truly understood Him."

The Brihadaranyaka Upanishad states:

Sa aesha neti netyatma agrihyoh (3.9.26)

"Depending on one's intellect, one can never understand God by one's own efforts"

The Ramayana states:

"Rama atarkya buddhi mana bani, mata hamara asa sunahi sayani" "Lord Sri Ramachandra is beyond the power of our intellect, mind and speech."

Again, if all these verses on the subject of knowing God clearly state that knowing Him is impossible, then how is Bhagavat Prapti possible? Sri Krishna is here explaining how to know Bhagavad Gnana. God bestows His divine knowledge on the living soul, then the blessed living soul who has received His grace can know Him. Yajurveda says this.

Tasya no Rasva Tasya no Dhehi

"No one can know the Lord without basking in the nectar born from His feet." Thus, true knowledge of God does not come from the exercise of our intellect, but only by His grace. Lord Krishna says that He does not choose the recipient of His grace, but He bestows it on those who unite their minds with devotion to Him. Next, he tells us what happens once we get the grace of Bhagavat.
word_by_word_meaning_english: tesham — to them; satata-yuktanam — always with strong will; bhajatam — for those engaged in devotion; preti-purukham — with love; dadami — I give; buddhi-yoga — divine knowledge; tam — that; yena — because of what; mam — to me; upayanti — comer; te — they.

sanskrit_sloka:
తేషామేవానుకంపార్థమ్ అహమజ్ఞానజం తమః
నాశయామ్యాత్మభావస్థొ జ్ఞానదీపేన భాస్వతా ।। 11 ।।
translation_english: With affection for them, I who am present in their hearts, will destroy the darkness created by ignorance with the bright lamp of knowledge.
explanation_english:
In this sloka, Lord Krishna further explains what Bhagavat Kripa is. Earlier, He had said that He would bestow His grace on those who engage their minds with love for Him and make Him the center of their plans, thoughts and activities. Now, he tells what happens when someone receives his grace. He says that he will destroy the darkness in their hearts with the lamp of knowledge.

Ignorance is often compared to darkness. But what is this lamp of knowledge that God refers to? At present our senses, mind and intellect are all natural, but God is divine. So we cannot see Him, hear Him, know Him or become one with Him. When the Lord bestows His grace, He bestows His divine yogic power on that soul. That is called pure sattva, which is different from maya sattva guna. When we get that pure sattva guna shakti, our senses, mind and intellect become divine. Simply put, by His grace, the Lord bestows His divine senses, divine mind and divine intellect upon the living soul. The pidapa, that living soul, who possesses these divine accessories, can see God, hear God, and become one with God. So, as the Vedanta darshan says: Vishesanugrahashcha (3.4.38)". It is by the grace of God that one attains divine knowledge." Accordingly, the divine energy of Himself is the lamp that Sri Krishna exemplifies. The darkness of material energy is dispelled by the light of God's divine energy.

sanskrit_sloka:
అర్జున ఉవాచ ।
పరం బ్రహ్మ పరం ధామ పవిత్రం పరమం భవాన్ ।
పురుషం శాశ్వతం దివ్యమ్ ఆదిదేవమజం విభుమ్ ।। 12 ।।

ఆహుస్త్వామృషయః  సర్వే దేవర్షిర్నారదస్తథా ।
అసితో దేవలో వ్యాసః  స్వయం చైవ బ్రవీషి మే ।। 13 ।।
translation_english: Arjuna said: Thou art the Parabrahma, the Parandham, the Supreme Holy One, the eternal God, the primordial man, the birthless and the supreme. Sages like Narada, Asita, Devala and Vyasa have declared this, and now you yourself are declaring this to me.
explanation_english:
Commentators on the Vedic scriptures like to say that Sri Krishna, Sri Rama etc. are not the Supreme Lord. The Supreme Being, a nirguna formless essence, assumes the same forms and manifests itself as incarnations, hence these incarnations are said to be one step below God. But, Arjuna refutes these views and says that Sri Krishna is the supreme cause in his incarnation.

After hearing the previous four shlokas Arjuna had full faith in the supremacy of Lord Sri Krishna; And he is expressing strongly outwardly the conviction he now has. When the wise say that knowledge is true, then its credibility is established. Sages have complete mastery over spiritual knowledge. That is why Arjuna mentions those sages - like Narada, Asita, Devala and Vyasa who say that Sri Krishna is the Supreme Lord and the All Cause. There is a poem in the Bhishma Parvam of the Mahabharata, in which many praise Lord Krishna. Sage Narada says: "Sri Krishna is the creator of all the worlds and the knower of the feelings of all minds. He is the Lord of all the deities who preside over this universe." (Sloka 68.2). Sage Markandeya states: "Lord Krishna is the goal and essence of all sacrifices. He is the past-present-future of everything." (Sloka 68.3) Sage Bhrigu said: "He is the God of God and the primordial incarnation of Lord Vishnu." (Sloka 68.4). Sage Veda Vyasa stated: "O Krishna, you are the Lord of the Vasus, you are the giver of power to Indra and other gods." (Sloka 68.5). Sage Angira said: "Shri Krishna is the creator of all beings. The springs are in His belly. He is the Supreme Lord." (Sloka 68.6). Elsewhere in the Mahabharata itself, Sage Asita and Devalu declare: "Sri Krishna is the creator of Lord Brahma who created the universe." (Mahabharata Vanaparvam 12.50). Arjuna, quoting these supreme authentic mahatmas - now says that by saying that Sri Krishna himself is the cause of all things - he himself confirms their words.

sanskrit_sloka:
సర్వమేతదృతం మన్యే యన్మాం వదసి కేశవ ।
న హి తే భగవన్ వ్యక్తిం విదుర్దేవా న దానవాః  ।। 14 ।।
translation_english: O Krishna, I believe with firm faith that everything you have said is true.  O Lord, neither the gods nor the demons can know your real form.
explanation_english:
Pidapa, who had briefly listened intently to the divine glories and infinite exaltation of Sri Krishna, Arjuna grew eager to hear more. Shri Krishna is still telling his glories, he has full faith and trust in God. Arjuna's intention in using the word "Yat" is that he believes that everything Sri Krishna says from the seventh chapter to the ninth chapter is true. Sri Krishna assures that everything said is true and is not a fanciful interpretation. Sri Krishna is addressed as Bhagavan, which means Supreme Lord. The word Bhagavan is mentioned in Devi Bhagavata Purana as follows.

Aishwaryasya Agungsya Dharmasya Yasasa Sasriya: Jnanavairagyoschaiva Shannam Bhagavanih

"Bhagavan is the one who possesses these six treasures in infinite measure - power, knowledge, beauty, prosperity, opulence and dispassion." Gods, demons and humans all have limited intelligence. They cannot know the complete philosophy of Bhagavat.

sanskrit_sloka:
స్వయమేవాత్మనాత్మానం వేత్థ త్వం పురుషోత్తమ ।
భూతభావన భూతేశ దేవదేవ జగత్పతే ।। 15 ।।
translation_english: O Purushottam, Creator of all things, Sarvabhutesa, Devdeva, Jagatpathe! In fact, you only know yourself through your own transcendental power.
explanation_english:
Declaring that Sri Krishna is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Arjuna addresses him thus:

bhuta-bhavana -- creator of all beings, universal father; bhutesa -- lord of all demons, supreme appointee; jagat-pate -- lord of all creation; deva-deva -- god of gods;

The Svetasvatara Upanishad mentions the same thing:

Yasmat param naparamasti kinchid (3.9)

"God can never be outdone; He is beyond all."

It has been said in the previous hymn that God cannot be known by anyone. This is clearly logical. All living entities (Jivatmans) have limited intellect, but God is infinite, so He is beyond the scope of their intellect. This makes Him nothing less; Rightly it will keep him in a high position. Western philosopher F.A. Jacobi states: "The God we know is not God." But, what Arjuna is saying in this hymn is that in the end, there is only one who knows what God is, He is God Himself. Thus, only Lord Krishna knows who/what He is, and if He bestows His energies on any living soul, that fortunate living soul can also know Him.

sanskrit_sloka:
వక్తుమర్హస్యశేషేణ దివ్యా హ్యాత్మవిభూతయః ।
యాభిర్విభూతిభిర్లోకాన్ ఇమాంస్త్వం వ్యాప్య తిష్ఠసి ।। 16 ।।

కథం విద్యామహం యోగిన్ త్వాం సదా పరిచింతయన్ ।
కేషు కేషు చ భావేషు చింత్యోఽసి భగవన్మయా ।। 17 ।।
translation_english: Please explain to me Your Divine Vibhutas in which You pervade and reside in all the worlds. O Yogeshwara, how can I know and remember You? And in what forms can I contemplate You, O Lord, while meditating?
explanation_english: Yogam here means yogamaya (the divine power of God), and yogi means the master of yogamaya.  Arjuna understood that Sri Krishna is Lord.   Now he wants to know the things that have not yet been told, how the manifestations of Sri Krishna will be revealed in this world. He longed to hear about the glories and the supreme status of Sri Krishna as the controller of the entire universe. That is why he prays like this, "I want to know Your Divine Lilas so that I may be granted unceasing devotion. But, without Your grace, it is impossible to know Your Personality. So, please, by Your grace, make me understand Your glories."

sanskrit_sloka:
విస్తరేణాత్మనో యోగం విభూతిం చ జనార్ధన ।
భూయః కథయ తృప్తిర్హి  శృణ్వతో నాస్తి మేఽమృతమ్  ।। 18 ।।
translation_english: Again recount Your divine glories and incarnations in abundance, O Janardhana.  If you listen to your nectar, it will never fade away.
explanation_english:
Arjuna here says "...listening to your nectar like nectar," instead of "...listening to your nectar." He left out the part "such are your words". This is a process called 'exaggeration' in literature, in which the allegorical object is abandoned. Sri Krishna is also addressed as Janardana, meaning "the kindhearted one to whom distressed people go for relief".

Stories describing God's glories are like nectar to those who love Him. So far he has been drinking in the words of the immortal Lord Krishna with his ears, and now "One more time...! My thirst to hear your Divine Lilas is still unquenched." He is encouraging him by saying that. This is the nature of Divyamrita. It satisfies on the one hand and at the same time leaves you wanting more. The Naimisaranya sages, while listening to the Srimad Bhagavatam from Suta Mahamuni, said the same thing:

Vayam tu na vithripyama uttamslokavikrameyachrinvatam rasagnanam savadu savadu repeatedly (1.1.19)

"For a devotee of Lord Krishna, listening to His Divine Leelas is never enough or boring. The quality of this Leelamrita grows as one experiences it."

sanskrit_sloka:
శ్రీ భగవానువాచ ।
హంత తే కథయిష్యామి దివ్యా హ్యత్మవిభూతయః ।
ప్రాధాన్యతః కురుశ్రేష్ఠ నాస్త్యంతో విస్తరస్య మే ।। 19 ।।
translation_english: Sri Bhagavanu said: Now I will briefly explain to you, O great son, my divine visions, for there is no end to their description.
explanation_english:
Amara Kosha (a popular ancient Sanskrit dictionary) defines the word vibhuti as "vibhutir bhutir aishwaryam", power and wealth". God's powers and opulences are infinite. In fact, everything about him is infinite. He has infinite forms, infinite names, infinite abodes, infinite incarnations, infinite lilas, There are innumerable devotees like this, so the Vedas call Him infinite.

Anantashchatma Visvarupo Hyakarta (Setasvatara Upanishad 1.9)

"God is infinite and manifests in this universe in innumerable forms. Even though He maintains this universe, He is akarta."

The Ramayana states:

Hari Ananta Hari Katha Ananta

"God is infinite and the leelas He performs in His infinite incarnations are also infinite." Sage Vedic Vyasa puts it more emphatically:

Yo va anantasya gunananantan anukramishyan satu bala-buddhihrajamsi bhumer ganayet kathanchit kalena naivakhilasakti dhamnah (Bhagavatam 11.4.2)

"Those who think they can count the glories of God are lesser Buddhas. One can count the specks of dust on this earth but cannot count the infinite glories of the Lord.” So, Sri Krishna says that here I am going to describe only a small part of His Vibhutas.

sanskrit_sloka:
అహమాత్మా గుడాకేశ సర్వభూతాశయస్థితః ।
అహమాదిశ్చ మధ్యం చ భూతానామంత ఏవ చ ।। 20 ।।
translation_english: O Arjuna, I am seated in the hearts of all demons. I am the beginning, middle and end of all beings.
explanation_english:
శ్రీ కృష్ణుడు, తాను జీవుడికి ఏమీ అంత దూరంగా వేరుగా లేను అని అంటున్నాడు - నిజానికి అతి దగ్గర కంటే దగ్గరగా ఉన్నాడు. నిత్య శాశ్వత ఆత్మ అన్ని ప్రాణుల హృదయ స్థానం లో స్థితమై ఉన్నది. వేదములు అంటున్నాయి: య ఆత్మని తిష్ఠతి , "భగవంతుడు మన ఆత్మ లోయందు స్థితమై ఉన్నాడు." అందులో కూర్చుని ఆ ఆత్మకు జీవశక్తి మరియు నిత్యశాశ్వత గుణము ప్రసాదిస్తాడు. ఆయన శక్తిని ఉపసంహరిస్తే, మన ఆత్మ కూడా జడమైపోతుంది మరియు నశించిపోతుంది. ఈ ప్రకారంగా మనం జీవాత్మలము, మన స్వీయ శక్తి చేత నిత్యులము మరియు చైతన్యవంతులము కాలేదు, పరమ చైతన్య వంతుడు మరియు సనాతనుడు అయిన భగవంతుడు మనలోనే (జీవాత్మ లోనే) ఉండి, తన శక్తిని మనకు ప్రసాదించటం చేత అలా ఉండగలుగుతున్నాము. కాబట్టి శ్రీ కృష్ణుడు సమస్త ప్రాణుల హృదయములో తాను స్థితుడనై ఉన్నాను అని అంటున్నాడు.

మన ఆత్మ భగవంతుని శరీరము, ఆయనే మన ఆత్మకి పరమాత్మ. భాగవతం ఇలా పేర్కొంటున్నది:

హరిర్హి సాక్షాద్భగవాన్ శరీరిణామాత్మా ఝాషాణామివ తోయమీప్సితం (5.18.13)

"భగవంతుడు సర్వ ప్రాణుల ఆత్మ కు ఆత్మ." మరల భాగవతంలో, గోపికలు తమ సొంత బిడ్డలను వదిలి పసివాడైన శ్రీ కృష్ణుడిని చూడటానికి వెళ్ళటం గురించి శుకదేవ పరమహంస చెప్పినప్పుడు, పరీక్షిత్తు, ఇది ఎలా సాధ్యం?అని అడిగాడు:

బ్రహ్మన్ పరోద్భవే కృష్ణే ఇయాన్ ప్రేమా కథం భవేత్ (10.14.49)

"ఓ బ్రాహ్మణా, అందరూ తల్లులూ తమ సొంత బిడ్డలపైనే మమకారం తో ఉంటారు. మరి గోపికలకు, తమ సొంత బిడ్డల పైన కూడా లేకుండా, ఈ యొక్క శ్రీ కృష్ణుడి పట్ల ఇంత గాఢమైన అనురక్తి ఎలా ఏర్పడినది? " శుకదేవ పరమహంస ఇలా బదులిచ్చాడు:

కృష్ణమేనమవేహి త్వమాత్మానమఖిలాత్మనాం (భాగవతం 10.14.55)

"శ్రీ కృష్ణుడు విశ్వములోని సర్వ ప్రాణులకు పరమాత్మ అని దయచేసి అర్థంచేసుకోండి. మానవ జాతి మేలు కోసం, తన యోగమాయా శక్తి ద్వారా ఒక మనుష్య రూపంలో అవతరించాడు."

శ్రీ కృష్ణుడు ఇంకా ఏమంటున్నాడంటే, తానే సమస్త జీవ భూతముల మొదలు, మధ్య, తుది (ఆది-మధ్య-అంతము) అని. అవి ఆయన నుండే ఉద్బవించాయి, కాబట్టి ఆయనే మొదలు. సృష్టి యందు వసించే అంతా జీవము ఆయన శక్తి చేతనే సంరక్షించి కొనసాగింపబడుతున్నది, కాబట్టి ఆయనే మధ్య. మరియు మోక్షము పొందిన వారు ఆయన యొక్క దివ్య ధామమునకు వెళ్లి, ఆయన సన్నిధిలోనే నిత్యశాశ్వతంగా నివసిస్తారు. అందుకే భగవంతుడే అన్ని ప్రాణులకు తుది. వేదములలో ఇవ్వబడిన భగవంతుని యొక్క నిర్వచనాలలో, ఒకటి ఈ క్రింద పేర్కొనబడినది.

యతో వా ఇమాని భూతాని జాయంతే, యేన జాతాని జీవంతి, యత్ప్రయంత్యభిసంవిశంతి(తైత్తిరీయ ఉపనిషత్తు 3.1.1)

"ఎవని నుండి సర్వ ప్రాణులు ఉద్భవించాయో వాడే భగవంతుడు; ఎవని యందు సర్వ ప్రాణులు ఆధారపడి స్థితమై ఉన్నాయో వాడే భగవంతుడు; ఎవని లోనికి సర్వ ప్రాణులు ఏకమై పోతాయో వాడే భగవంతుడు."
word_by_word_meaning_english: Aham — I; atma — soul; Gudakesha — Arjuna, conqueror of sleep; sarva-bhuta — of all the demons; ashaya-sthitah — seated in the heart; Aham — I; adih — beginning; Cha — and; Madhyam — middle; Cha — and; bhutanam — of all the bhutams; antah — final (end); eva — also; Cha — and.

sanskrit_sloka:
ఆదిత్యానామహం విష్ణుః జ్యోతిషాం రవిరంశుమాన్ ।
మరీచిర్మరుతామస్మి  నక్షత్రాణామహం శశీ ।। 21 ।।
translation_english: Of Aditi's twelve sons I am Vishnu; I am the sun among bright things. I am the moon among the stars of the night sky and the maruthu among the maruts.
explanation_english:
What we know from Puranas is that Kasyapa Mahama had two wives - Aditi and Diti. Through his first wife Aditi he had twelve gods, namely - Dhata, Mitra, Aryama, Sakra, Varuna, Amsa, Bhaga, Vivasvana, Pusha, Savita, Tvashta and Vamana. Among them Vamanu is an incarnation of Lord Vishnu. Thus, Krishna claims to be declaring his glory as Vishnu (in Vamana form) among the Adityas (the twelve sons of Aditi).

The sun is supreme among the bright ones. The Ramayana states:

Rakapati shodasa uahim taragana samudaisakala girinha dava laia binu rabi rati na jai

"All the lights of the night, all the stars in the sky, even the moon - they are not enough to dispel the darkness of the night. But, the moment the sun rises, the darkness of the night is dispelled." Such is the power of the sun, Sri Krishna declares that it is his Vibhuti.

Next he talks about the night sky. There is a famous saying, "A single moon is better than a thousand stars". Among the stars and casts in the sky at night, he calls the moon itself, which well declares the vibhuti of Sri Krishna.

What else we can learn from the Puranas is that Kashyapa fathered Daityas (demons) through his second wife, Diti. But, even after the Daityas, Diti asked for another son who was more powerful than Indra (Lord of the Gods). She kept her child in her womb for a year. Indra cut the fetus into many pieces with a diamond weapon, but it turned into many embryos. These are the Maruts, i.e. the 49 types of gases circulating in this universe that are very beneficial. The main ones are avaha, pravaha, nivaha, purvaha, udvaha, samvaha and parivaha. Among these, another important process is called Marichi. Shri Krishna says that in the gases, His Vibhuti is manifested in the form of Marichi.
word_by_word_meaning_english: adityanam — among the twelve sons of Aditi; Aham — I; Vishnuh — the form of Vishnu; Jyotisham — in bright objects; ravih — the sun; anshu-man — bright; marichih — forgotten; marutham — among the Maruts; asmi — I; nakshatraana — in the stars; Aham — I; Sasih — the moon.

sanskrit_sloka:
వేదానాం సామవేదోఽస్మి దేవానామస్మి వాసవః ।
ఇంద్రియాణాం మనశ్చాస్మి  భూతానామస్మి చేతనా ।। 22 ।।
translation_english: I am Sama Veda among the Vedas, Indra among the gods. the mind in the senses; Consciousness in animals.
explanation_english:
There are four Vedic divisions - Rigveda, Yajurveda, Samaveda, Atharvaveda. Among these, the Sama Veda describes the glories of God as manifested in the deities who preside over the universe. The Sama Veda is musically very charming and is sung in praise of the Lord. It is very endearing to those who understand it and instills devotion in those who hear it.

Vasava is another name for Lord of Gods Indra. There is no being who can match Him in glory, power, and status. As a result of many births of meritorious deeds, any living soul is given the position of Indra. Thus, Indra is indicative of the radiant Vibhuti of the Lord.

The five senses function properly only when the mind is present. If the mind wanders, the senses cannot function properly. For example, the ears can hear what others are saying, but if the mind is distracted while they are talking, we cannot understand what they are saying. Therefore, the mind is the king of the senses. Sri Krishna says about it that it proves his power; And earlier in the Bhagavad Gita, he states that the mind is the most important sixth sense. (Sloka 15.7).

Consciousness is an attribute of the soul, distinct from inert matter. The difference between a living person and a dead person is that the living person has consciousness and the dead person does not. Consciousness in the soul is due to the divine power of God. Thus, the Vedas state: chetanaschetananam (Kathopanishad 2.2.13) "Consciousness is the Lord of the conscious."
word_by_word_meaning_english: vedanam — in the Vedas; sama-vedah — the sama veda; asmi — I; devanam — among the deities; asmi — I; vasavah — Indra; indriyanam — in the senses; manah — the mind; Cha — and; asmi — I; bhutanam — among creatures; asmi — I; Chetana — consciousness.

sanskrit_sloka:
రుద్రాణాం శంకరశ్చాస్మి విత్తేశో యక్షరక్షసామ్ ।
వసూనాం పావకశ్చాస్మి మేరుః శిఖరిణామహమ్ ।। 23 ।।
translation_english: Among the Rudras I am Shankara; Kubera is among the Asuras; Agni is among the Vasus and Meru is among the mountains.
explanation_english:
Rudras are the eleven forms of Lord Shiva - Hara, Bahurupa, Tryambaka, Aparajita, Vrisakapi, Sankara, Kapardi, Raivata, Mrigavyadha, Sarva, Kapali. They are called by different names in different places in Puranas. Among these, Shankara is the root form of Shiva in the universe.

Yakshas (partly divine Asuras), who love to promote and hide wealth. Their leader was Kubera, the god of wealth and treasurer of the gods. He thus declares the glory of the Lord among the demons.

There are Ashta (eight) vasus - earth, water, fire, air, sky, sun, moon and stars. These are the source of the gross structure of the universe. Of these, Agni provides heat and energy to the rest. That is why Sri Krishna says it is his special Vibhuti.

Mount Meru is famous in the heavenly worlds for its natural wealth. It is believed that many celestial planets revolve around it having it as its axis. That is why Sri Krishna calls it his Vibhuti.  Just as wealth makes a rich man great, all these glories declare the glory of God.
word_by_word_meaning_english: rudranam — among the Rudras; Shankarah — Shiva (Lord Shankara); Cha — and; asmi — I; vitta-esah — goddess of wealth and treasurer of the gods; yaksha — the yakshas; rakshasam — among the demons; vasunam — in the sums; pavakah — fire; Cha — and; asmi — I; meruh — Mount Meru; shikharinam — in the mountains; Aham — I.

sanskrit_sloka:
పురోధసాం చ ముఖ్యం మాం విద్ధి పార్థ బృహస్పతిమ్ ।
సేనానీనామహం స్కందః సరసామస్మి సాగరః ।। 24 ।।
translation_english: Among the priests I am Jupiter; Among soldiers I am Karthike; And in the reservoirs know that I am the ocean.
explanation_english:
Priests perform pujadi ritual kandas in temples and homes. Jupiter is the chief priest in the heavenly world. That is why he is the most important among the priests. Here Sri Krishna says that he is Jupiter among all priests. But, in Srimad Bhagavatam verse 11.16.22, Sri Krishna says that he is Vashishta among priests. Why did he say differently in these two places? What this suggests is that we should not give priority to the object, but to the Vibhuti of God manifested in that object. This is how we should understand all the glorious objects/persons mentioned by Sri Krishna. Priority should not be given to the object, but to the vibhuti of God manifested in that object.

Kartikeya, the son of Shiva, the commander of the army of gods, is also known as Skanda. That is why he is the head of all armies, and well proclaims the glory of God. Moreover, Sri Krishna also says that among the unflowing reservoirs, He is the mighty great ocean.
word_by_word_meaning_english: purodhasam — among the priests; Cha — and; important — chiefs; mam — I; viddhi — know; Partha — Arjuna, O son of Pritha; brihaspatim — Jupiter; senaninam — among the generals; Aham — I; skandah — Kartikeya; sarasam — in reservoirs; asmi — I; sagarah — ocean.

sanskrit_sloka:
మహార్షీణాం భృగురహం గిరామస్మ్యేకమక్షరమ్ ।
యజ్ఞానాం జపయజ్ఞోఽస్మి స్థావరాణాం హిమాలయః ।। 25 ।।
translation_english: I am Bhrigu Maharshi among sages and 'Om' is the transcendental of sounds. I am chanting the Lord's name again and again in japas (sacrifices); I am the Himalayas among the settlements;
explanation_english:
అన్ని పండ్లు మరియు పూలు ఒకే నేల నుండి పెరిగినా, వాటిలో కొన్నింటిని మాత్రమే ప్రదర్శనకు ఉంచుతారు. అదే విధంగా, ఈ విశ్వములో వ్యక్తమయిన లేదా అవ్యక్తమయిన ప్రతిదీ కూడా భగవంతుని విభూతియే, కానీ వాటిలో ఉన్న ప్రధానమైన వాటిని వేరుగా ఆయన వైభవముగా చూపిస్తారు.

స్వర్గాది లోకములలో ఉన్న ఋషులలో భృగు మహర్షి ప్రత్యేకమైన వాడు. ఆయనకు జ్ఞానము, యశస్సు మరియు భక్తి ఉన్నాయి. విష్ణు మూర్తి తన వక్ష స్థలం మీద ఆయన పాద గుర్తు కలిగి ఉన్నాడు. భృగు మహర్షి, త్రిమూర్తులైన బ్రహ్మ, విష్ణు, శివులను పరీక్షించటం అనే, పురాణాలలో చెప్పబడిన ఒక దివ్య లీల పర్యవసానంగా ఇది జరిగింది. శ్రీ కృష్ణుడి విభూతి ఆయన ద్వారా చక్కగా ప్రకటితమవుతున్నది.

భగవంతుడిని నిరాకార రూపంలో ఆరాధన చేసేవారు, "ఓం" కారపు ధ్వని పై ధ్యానం చేస్తుంటారు, ఇది భగవంతుని ఇంకొక విభూతి. శ్రీ కృష్ణుడు ఇంతకు క్రితమే 7.8వ మరియు 8.13వ శ్లోకాలలో, "ఓం" కారము పవిత్రమైన శబ్దము అని చెప్పి ఉన్నాడు. అది 'అనాహత నాదము' (ఈ జగత్తు మొత్తం వ్యాపించి ఉన్న శబ్ద ప్రకంపన). తరచుగా "ఓం" కారము వేద మంత్రముల ప్రారంభంలో పవిత్రత కోసం ఉచ్చరించబడుతుంది. ఈ యొక్క "ఓం" కారము నుండే గాయత్రీ మంత్రము ప్రకటించబడినది అని అంటారు, మరియు గాయత్రీ మంత్రము నుండే వేదములు ప్రకటితమయినాయి.

హిమాలయములు ఉత్తర భారత దేశంలో ఉన్న పర్వత శ్రేణులు. యుగాల నుండి అవి కోట్లమంది భక్తులలో ఆధ్యాత్మిక ఉత్తేజాన్ని కలిగించాయి. వాటి వాతావరణం, పర్యావరణం మరియు ఏకాంతము, ఆధ్యాత్మిక పురోగతి కోసం సాధన కు ఏంతో అనుకూలముగా ఉంటాయి. అందుకే, ఏంతో మంది మహర్షులు హిమాలయములలో వారి సూక్ష్మ శరీరాలలో, వారి స్వీయ పురోగతి కోసం మరియు మానవ జాతి సంక్షేమం కోసం తపస్సు ఆచరిస్తూ నివసిస్తుంటారు. అందుకే, ప్రపంచంలో ఉన్న ఎన్నెన్నో పర్వత శ్రేణులలో కంటే హిమాలయములే భగవంతుని యొక్క వైభవాన్ని చక్కగా ప్రదర్శిస్తున్నాయి.

యజ్ఞము అంటే మనలను ఆ భగవంతునికి అంకితం చేసుకునే ప్రక్రియ. అన్ని యజ్ఞములకంటే సరళమైనది భగవంతుని పవిత్ర నామములను జపించటమే. దీనినే జప యజ్ఞము అంటారు; అంటే నిరంతరం భక్తితో భగవంతుని దివ్య నామాలను పదే పదే అంటూ ఉండటమే. కర్మకాండ విధాన యజ్ఞములు ఆచరించటానికి, ఏంతో నిష్ఠ గా పాటించవలసిన ఎన్నో నియమాలు ఉంటాయి. కాని, జప యజ్ఞములో, ఎలాంటి నియమాలు లేవు. దాన్ని ఎక్కడైనా, ఎప్పుడైనా చేయవచ్చు, మరియు అది మిగతా రకాల యజ్ఞముల కన్నా పవిత్రమైనది. ఈ ప్రస్తుత కలి యుగంలో, భగవంతుని నామ జపం చేయమని మరింత ధృడంగా చెప్పబడింది.

కలియుగ కేవల నామ ఆధారా, సుమిరి సుమిరి నర ఉతరహి( పారా (రామాయణం)

"కలి యుగంలో భగవంతుడి నామ జపము మరియు స్మరణము భవ సాగరాన్ని దాటటానికి ఉన్న శక్తి వంతమైన సాధనము."

sanskrit_sloka:
అశ్వత్థః సర్వవృక్షాణాం దేవర్షీణాం చ నారదః ।
గంధర్వాణాం చిత్రరథః సిద్ధానాం కపిలో మునిః ।। 26 ।।
translation_english: Among the trees I am the Ravi tree; Narada is among the gods. Among the Gandharvas I am Chitrarathu, among the Siddhas I am Kapila Muni.
explanation_english:
It gives a cool and peaceful feeling to those who sit under the Ravi tree. As it expands through the fronds it is larger and provides cooler shade over a larger area. Buddha meditated under a Ravi tree and attained enlightenment.

Devarshi Narada was the teacher of many Mahatmas like Veda Vyasa, Valmiki, Dhruva and Prahlad. He is always glorifying the glories of God and doing divine works in high places.  He has a reputation for creating conflicts whenever he wants; Sometimes people misunderstand him as a trouble maker. But, in his desire to uplift the glorified, he creates strife around them, which leads to their introspection and purification.

In the Gandharva world there are those who sing wonderfully, and the best singer among them is Chitraratha. Siddhas are Yogis who have attained spiritual perfection. Among them Kapila Muni expounded the philosophy of Samkhya Shastra and taught the uniqueness of Bhakti Yoga. (This is described in Srimad Bhagavatam 3rd Skanda). He is an incarnation of Bhagwat, hence Sri Krishna refers to him here as proclaiming his glories.

sanskrit_sloka:
ఉచ్చైఃశ్రవసమశ్వానాం విద్ధి మామమృతోద్భవమ్ ।
ఐరావతం గజేంద్రాణాం నరాణాం చ నరాధిపమ్ ।। 27 ।।
translation_english: Amongst the horses, I, born of the Amrita Samudra, am Uchchaihsravasam. Among the Gajendras I am Airavata and the king of men.
explanation_english: Shri Krishna continues to name the excellent in every department to convey His glory/glory. Uccaihsravasamu is a winged horse in the deva worlds belonging to Indra, the king of devas. It is white in color and is the fastest horse in the universe.  It originated in Samudra Madhana Lila of Devas and Asuras.  Airavata is a white gaja (elephant) which is the vehicle of Indra.  It is also called Ardha-Mathanga, meaning "the elephant in the clouds".

sanskrit_sloka:
ఆయుధానామహం వజ్రం ధేనూనామస్మి కామధుక్ ।
ప్రజనశ్చాస్మి కందర్పః సర్పాణామస్మి వాసుకిః ।। 28 ।।
translation_english: Vajrayudham among weapons and Kamadhenu among cows. I am Kamadeva (Cupid) among the causes of fertility; I am Vasuki among the serpents.
explanation_english:
The sacrifices of the great Dadhichi mentioned in the Puranas are unmatched in history. Once Indra, the king of gods, was chased out of heaven by a demon named Vrittasura.  The demon had the boon of being unkillable by any weapon that existed until then.  Undeterred, Indra sought Shiva's help, and Shiva took him to Vishnu Murti.  What Vishnu Murthy told Indra was that only a diamond weapon made from Dadhichi Muni bomikas could kill Vrittasura.  Indra then prayed to Dadhichi Muni to sacrifice his life in order to use his bones to make the Vajrayudham. Dadhichi forgave it but wanted to go on a pilgrimage to all the rivers first.  In order to fulfill Dadhichi's wish, Indra then wasted no time and brought the waters of all the holy rivers to Naimisaranya.  Afterwards, Dadhichi left his body through the process of yoga. A diamond weapon made from his bomikas was used to defeat Vrittasuri. With this Indra regained the position of lord of heaven. Here, Sri Krishna is referring to the Vajrayudham as an indicator of God's splendor (vibhuti) even more than the wheel, the mace, which is always near the Vishnu murti.

Sri Krishna also says in this sloka that Maithuna Kriya is not impure when it is done only for the sake of good offspring.  Kamadeva (Cupid) is responsible for the force of attraction between men and women necessary to perpetuate the human race through procreation. This sexual desire has its origin in God, and it should not be misused for sense gratification, but only for procreation. In verse 7.11, Sri Krishna declares that sexual desire is not unscientific and unethical.

sanskrit_sloka:
అనంతశ్చాస్మి నాగానాం వరుణో యాదసామహమ్ ।
పితౄణామర్యమా చాస్మి యమః సంయమతామహమ్ ।। 29 ।।
translation_english: Among Nagas I am infinite; Varuna is among those who live in water. I am Arya in Pitrgana;  I am Yamadharmaraja among those who give the rule of Nyaya-Dharma.
explanation_english:
Ananta (Adi Sheshu) means the cobra on which Lord Vishnu sleeps. He has ten thousand beds.  He has been singing the glories of God with every head since the beginning of creation but the description is said to be incomplete.

Varuna means sea god. Arya means the third son of Aditi. He is worshiped as the leader of patriarchs. Yama means the god of death.  Pidapa takes care of removing the soul from the body of the deceased. According to what the soul has done in this life, the punishments or Uttamgatas in the next life will be given on behalf of the Lord. No matter how terrible and painful they are, he does not deviate even a little from his dharma.  He declares the glory/vibhuti of God as the provider of absolute flawless justice.

sanskrit_sloka:
ప్రహ్లాదశ్చాస్మి దైత్యానాం కాలః కలయతామహమ్ ।
మృగాణాం చ మృగేంద్రోఽహం వైనతేయశ్చ పక్షిణామ్ ।। 30 ।।
translation_english: Among the giants I do not rejoice; I am time, which controls everything. Know that I am the lion among beasts and the eagle among birds.
explanation_english:
Prahlad was born as the son of the demon king Hiranyakasipu, who was a mighty warrior. But, he became one of the greatest Vishnu devotees. Hence, among the demons, Prahlada proclaims the Vibhuti of the Lord. Time subsumes even the strongest and greatest entities in the universe.

The majestic lion is the king of the jungle, and the power of God among animals is manifested in the lion. Garuda (Garutman) is the divine vehicle of Lord Vishnu and the greatest of all birds.

sanskrit_sloka:
పవనః పవతామస్మి రామః శస్త్రభృతామహమ్ ।
ఝషాణాం మకరశ్చాస్మి స్రోతసామస్మి జాహ్నవీ ।। 31 ।।
translation_english: I am a gas among the holy ones; Rama is among the surgeons. Among the aquatic animals is the Makara (crocodile), and among the flowing rivers is the Ganges.
explanation_english:
In nature, Vayu (air) performs the work of sanctification very well. It turns impure water into water vapor; Anything on earth carries a stench; Gives oxygen (breath) and makes fire burn. Thus it is a great holy monastic substance in nature.

Sri Ramachandra Prabhu is one of the most powerful warriors on earth and his bow is the most lethal weapon.  Yet never once did he abuse his superior position. Whenever he uses a weapon, it is only for good. That is why he is the best among surgeons. Rama is also an incarnation of God, hence Sri Krishna refers to him as himself.

Born from the Lord's feet, the river Ganga is a sacred river. It descended from the heavenly worlds to the earth. Many great sages practiced austerities on the banks of that river, which further cemented the sanctity of its waters.  Unlike ordinary water, the water of the Ganges, if kept in a jar, does not spoil for years. In earlier times this was very noticeable, but in modern times this effect has been reduced slightly due to the addition of crores of liters of pollutants into the Ganges.

sanskrit_sloka:
సర్గాణామాదిరంతశ్చ మధ్యం చైవాహమర్జున ।
అధ్యాత్మ విద్యా విద్యానాం వాదః ప్రవదతామహమ్ ।। 32 ।।
translation_english: Know, O Arjuna, that I am the beginning, the middle and the end of all creation. In education I am the spiritual education, and in discussions I am the logical decision.
explanation_english:
Earlier in the 20th sloka, Sri Krishna had said that He is the beginning, middle and end of all beings. Now, he says the same thing to all creation, "All that is created, sky, air, fire, water and earth together is called Sarga. I am the creator (Adi), the state (middle) and the rhythm (end) of all these. Therefore, on the processes of creation, state and rhythm, they can be meditated upon as my Vibhuti."

Education is the scientific knowledge acquired by a person. The Shastras elaborate eighteen types of education. Among them, fourteen are important:

Angani vedashchatvaro mimamsa nyaya vastarah.puranam dharmashastra cha vidyahyeta schaturdasaayurvedo dhanurvedo gandharvaschaiva te trayaharthashastra chaturtham tu vidya hyashtadasaiva tah (Vishnu Purana 3.6.27-28)

"Siksha, Kalpa, Vyakarana, Nirukti, Jyotisha, Chandassu - these six are called Vedangas (parts of the Vedas). Rigveda, Yajurveda, Samaveda, Atharva Veda - these are the four branches of the Vedas. Together with Mimamsa, Nyaya, Dharma Shastras and Puranas there are fourteen main vidyas." Studying these vidyas enhances intellect, enhances knowledge and increases understanding of the path of Dharma. Moreover, spiritual knowledge frees human beings from material worldly bonds and bestows them with immortality. In this way, it is superior to the previous educations. The same thing is said in Sri Madbhagavatam: Sa Vidya Tanmatiraya (Sloka 4.29.49) "The best education is that which makes the mind attuned to the Lord's attributes".

In arguments and logic, jalpa means to find fault with the words of another in order to establish one's point of view. Vidandamu is just arguing pointlessly without giving a chance for a proper debate on the truth. Argument means giving a logical conclusion to a discussion. Logic is the main basis for exchanging ideas and establishing truth. Rational consciousness is the basis for the smooth development and instruction of knowledge in human society. Universal logical principles are proof of God's power.

sanskrit_sloka:
అక్షరాణామకారోఽస్మి ద్వంద్వః సామాసికస్య చ ।
అహమేవాక్షయః కాలో ధాతాహం విశ్వతోముఖః ।। 33 ।।
translation_english: A-karamanu in letters; Duality of problems in problems. I am the infinite time, and Brahman among the creators.
explanation_english:
All the alphabets in Sanskrit are also formed by combining the half letter with the letter "a". For example, "k + a = ka" (क + अ = क ; k + a = ka). So, a-kara is very important in Sanskrit alphabet. "A" is the first vowel in the alphabet, and since vowels are written before consonants, "A" is the first letter to appear.

Although Sanskrit is a very ancient language, it is highly civilized and sophisticated.  A common process in the Sanskrit language is to combine words to form a word. If two but more words lose their endings in making a compound word, the resulting word is called a compound word.  There are six prominent types of Samasas: 1) Dwandva 2) Bahuvrihi 3) Karma Dharaya 4) Tatpurusha 5) Dvigu 6) Avyayi Bhava. Of these duality is the best. Because two words have equal importance, in others, one word is dominant or two words combined give meaning to a third word. Radha-Krishna is an example of a dual term.  Sri Krishna famously declares it as his Vibhuti.

Creation is a process that is amazing and mesmerizing to watch. Even the most advanced technological inventions of the human race seem insignificant compared to creation. Therefore, Sri Krishna Paramatma says that Brahma Ye, who created the entire universe, by his creativity, the greatest of all creators, has displayed the glory of God.

sanskrit_sloka:
మృత్యుః సర్వహరశ్చాహమ్ ఉద్భవశ్చ భవిష్యతామ్ ।
కీర్తిః శ్రీర్వాక్చ నారీణాం స్మృతిర్మేధా ధృతిః క్షమా ।। 34 ।।
translation_english: I am the all-consuming death, I am the producer of all that is to come.  In female characteristics I am fame, wealth, fine speech, memory, intelligence, courage and forgiveness.
explanation_english:
There is a saying in English “as sure as death.” One who is born must die. All life inevitably ends in death, hence "dead end." There is also a saying. God not only has the power to create; He is also the power of destruction.  He devours everything in the form of death. In the cycle of birth and death, the dead are reborn. Sri Krishna says that he is also the strategist for what comes before.

Some qualities are said to adorn the personality of women, while others are said to be particularly admirable in men.  In fact, having these two types of qualities is a complete personality.  Here, Sri Krishna says that qualities - fame, wealth, good speech, memory, intelligence, courage and forgiveness - make women great.  The first three qualities of this are manifested externally, and the last four are manifested internally.

Apart from these, Prajapati Daksha, the progenitor of the human race, had twenty-four daughters. Five of these are considered the best women - Kirti, Smriti, Medha, Dhriti and Kshama.  She was the daughter of Bhrigu Maharshi named Sri. Vak is the daughter of Brahma.  These seven women, according to their names, are the presiding deities of the seven gunas mentioned in this hymn. Here, Sri Krishna refers to these qualities as his Vibhuti.

sanskrit_sloka:
బృహత్సామ తథా సామ్నాం గాయత్రీ ఛందసామహమ్ ।
మాసానాం మార్గశీర్షోఽహమ్ ఋతూనాం కుసుమాకరః ।। 35 ।।
translation_english: In the Sama Vedic mantras know that I am Brihatsama; Among the rhymes, Gayatri Chandasa is Nene. Margasirsha month in the Hindava almanac, and the spring that brings forth the flowers of the seasons.
explanation_english:
Earlier Sri Krishna had said that among the Vedas, Samaveda is the one with the most wonderful hymns. Now, in the Samaveda he says that he is Brihatsama with the best sweetness. It is usually sung at midnight.

The Sanskrit language, like other languages, has a distinctive rhyme and rhythm for writing poetry. The hymns/poems of the Vedas are in many rhymes. Gayatri Chandasa is the most attractive and sweet among them. One of the most important mantras in this chant is the Gayatri Mantra. This mantra has a very mystical meaning:

Bhurbhuvah svah tatsaviturvarenyam bhargo devasya dhimahi deo yo nah prachodayat (Rigveda 3.62.10)

"We meditate on that God who shines in the worlds and is adorable. He is the remover of all sins and the destroyer of ignorance. May He guide our intellect in the right path."

The Gayatri Mantra is a part of the upanayana samskara for boys, which is chanted daily during the dusk. In Vedas we also find Gayatri Mantras - Devi Gayatri, Rudra Gayatri, Brahma Gayatri, Paramahamsa Gayatri and many more.

Margasirsha is the ninth month in the Hindu calendar. It comes in the months of November-December. The temperature in India is neither too hot nor too cold at that time. It is harvest time in the agricultural fields. That is why it is a very favorite month for people.

Spring is called Ritu-raju (the king of seasons). It is a time when nature, delightfully, manifests its vitality. Many festivals are celebrated during the Vassata season while enjoying the bliss of the atmosphere. Thus, among the seasons, spring best expresses the vibhuti/aishwarya of the Lord.

sanskrit_sloka:
ద్యూతం  ఛలయతామస్మి తేజస్తేజస్వినామహమ్ ।
జయోఽస్మి వ్యవసాయోఽస్మి సత్త్వం సత్త్వవతామహమ్ ।। 36 ।।
translation_english: I am a gambler among cheaters; I am the brightest among the brightest. I am victory among the victorious, and determination among the determined, and virtue among the righteous.
explanation_english:
Sri Krishna claims not only the virtues but also vices as his Vibhuti. Gambling is a dangerous bad habit that destroys families, businesses and lives. Yudhisthira's weakness for gambling led to the Mahabharata war. And if gambling is also the glory of God, is it not harmful, and why is it forbidden?

The answer is that God bestows His power on the living soul, along with the freedom to choose to do whatever he likes. If we choose to forget Him, He gives us the power to forget. This way, electricity can be used for both heating and cooling the home. It is up to the consumer how they use that electricity. But the power station that supplied that power has nothing to do with whether the power is utilized or misused by the consumer. Similarly, gambling also has God-given intelligence and ability. But, if the gift given by God is misused, God is not responsible for those sinful deeds.

Everyone likes to succeed; It reveals the glory of God. Also, Sri Krishna gave great importance to the quality of strong will. This has been said earlier in verses 2.41, 2.44, and 9.30.  The goodness of good men is also a proof of God's power. All virtues, accomplishments, fame, success and determination - all these are derived from God. Instead of thinking that these are our own, we should note that they are from God.

sanskrit_sloka:
వృష్ణీనాం వాసుదేవోఽస్మి పాండవానాం ధనంజయః ।
మునీనామప్యహం వ్యాసః కవీనాముశనా కవిః ।। 37 ।।
translation_english: Among the descendants of Vrishni I am Krishna and among the Pandavas I am Arjuna. Know that Veda Vyasa is among the ancients and Shukracharya is among the great thinkers.
explanation_english:
Lord Krishna was born as the son of Vasudeva in the Vrishni clan in Bhu-loka. Since no soul is superior to the Lord, naturally, in the Vrishni lineage, He is the most glorious person.  Pandavas are the five sons of King Pandu - Yudhishthira, Bhima, Arjuna, Nakula and Sahadeva. Among them Arjuna was an incomparably gifted archer and a close devotee of Lord Krishna.  He considered God as his dear friend.

Veda Vyasa is of great importance among the ancients. He is also known as "Badarayana" and "Krishna Dwaipayana".  He expounded Vedic knowledge in many ways and wrote many Puranas for the welfare of human beings.  In fact, Veda Vyasa is an incarnation of Sri Krishna, and Veda Vyasa is mentioned as one of the avatars mentioned in Srimad Bhagavatam.

Shukracharya is a wise sage; He was renowned for his expertise in ethical/ritual sciences. Compassionate, he took the demons as his disciples and directed their progress. Because of his prowess he is said to be a God's Vibhuti.

sanskrit_sloka:
దండో దమయతామస్మి నీతిరస్మి జిగీషతామ్ ।
మౌనం చైవాస్మి గుహ్యానాం జ్ఞానం జ్ఞానవతామహమ్ ।। 38 ।।
translation_english: Among the measures to prevent injustice I am righteous punishment and good behavior among the ambitious. I am silent in secrets. I am the wisest of the wise.
explanation_english:
Human nature being what it is, preaching alone is not sufficient for good behavior among people. Punishment, judiciously administered at the right time, is an important tool that contributes to the training of good morals and the reformation of sinful behavior.  One of its objectives is to prevent those who are inclined to do bad things in the society.  Modern management theory tells us how a minutely appropriate punishment or even minutely rewarded can change the behavior of people.

The desire for success is universal, but those of steadfast integrity will not compromise ethics/honesty for it. Success achieved in a righteous way is proof of God's power.

A secret is something that is generally kept from the public for a purpose. There is a saying in the English language, "A secret known to one man is a secret; a secret known to two is no more a secret; and a secret known to three is like news told to the rest of the world." Thus the greatest mystery lies in silence.

As spiritual knowledge matures, one gets real knowledge through attainment of Atma or Bhagavat. It is the endowed person – who sees all events, people and things in relation to Bhagavat. Such knowledge sanctifies one, makes one perfect, satisfied and elevates one to a higher level.  It shows good direction in life, gives strength to endure ups and downs. It gives strength of will to persevere till the ultimate goal is achieved.  Sri Krishna says that He is the knowledge that is revealed among the wise.

sanskrit_sloka:
యచ్చాపి సర్వభూతానాం బీజం తదహమర్జున ।
న తదస్తి వినా యత్ స్యాన్మయా భూతం చరాచరమ్ ।। 39 ।।
translation_english: I, Arjuna, am the original productive seed of creation of all demons.  Not even a carnivorous creature is without Me.
explanation_english:
Sri Krishna is both the efficient cause and the material cause of all creation. Efficient cause means He is the creator who does the necessary work to create and manifest the world. Material cause means that the substance required for creation comes from Him. In verses 7.10 and 9.18, Sri Krishna declares himself as "Sanatana Bijamunu". Again here he also refers to himself as the "productive seed". He declares that He is the cause of all things, and that nothing can exist without His power.

Animals are born in four types: Oviparous - those born from eggs, such as birds, snakes and lizards;  uteri - those born from the mother's womb; such as humans, cows, dogs and cats; svedajamula - arising from sveda (sweat); ticks, , such as; Plants - things that grow from the earth such as trees, vines, grass and corn;  Apart from these there are other life forms like ghosts, ghosts and ghosts. Sri Krishna is the source of all these.

sanskrit_sloka:
నాంతోఽస్తి మమ దివ్యానాం విభూతీనాం పరంతప ।
ఏష తూద్దేశతః ప్రోక్తో విభూతేర్విస్తరో మయా ।। 40 ।।
translation_english: There is no end to my divine delights, O Parantapa. What I have said so far is only a small part of my infinite glories.
explanation_english:
Shri Krishna is now concluding his Vibhuts matter. From sloka 20 to sloka 30, he describes 82 of his infinite vibhutas. He states that only a part (uddesatah) of this whole thing (vistarah) is said.

If sarvamu isvara vibhuti, then there is a doubt that what is the need to say these things? The answer to this is that Arjuna was asking Sri Krishna and how he should be remembered/remembered, and then these glories (vibhuts) were explained. The mind naturally gravitates towards the extraordinary, and therefore God reveals the particularities of His glory. Whenever we see any extraordinary feature manifested anywhere, if we observe it as the effulgence of God, the mind naturally goes to Ishvara. But, if we look at the macro perspective, since there is glory of God in every thing, big or small, we should think that the whole world is giving us innumerable examples to increase our devotion. A paint company in India advertises like this, "Whenever you see colors think of us." It means, "Whenever you see colors, think of us". How can we understand what Sri Krishna is saying in this present case, "If you see anything wonderful anywhere, remember me".

sanskrit_sloka:
యద్యద్ విభూతిమత్సత్వం శ్రీమద్ ఊర్జితమేవ వా ।
తత్ తత్ దేవావగచ్చ  త్వం మమ తేజోఽశసంభవమ్ ।। 41 ।।
translation_english: If you see anything beautiful, anything wonderful, or anything powerful, know it as the taluk of My beauty.
explanation_english: Current flowing in the speaker generates sound from it. But, those who don't know the principle behind how it works may misunderstand that the sound is coming from the speaker itself. In the same way, whenever we see an extraordinary glory anywhere, that amazes us, makes us ecstatic, makes us happy, it should be understood as a taluka of God's glory.  God is infinite in beauty, power, wisdom and wealth. It is His power that gives all beings and all things their beauty. Thus, we should make our object of worship the Lord who is the origin of all-richness.

sanskrit_sloka:
అథవా బహునైతేన కిం జ్ఞాతేన తవార్జున ।
విష్టభ్యాహమిదం కృత్స్నమ్ ఏకాంశేన స్థితో జగత్ ।। 42 ।।
translation_english: What is the need for this vast knowledge, O Arjuna? Just know this, with just one tiny aspect of me, permeating the entire universe and sustaining it.
explanation_english:
ఆ ప్రశ్నకు ఇంతకుక్రితమే సమాధానం చెప్పేసాను అన్న అర్థాన్ని శ్రీ కృష్ణుడి మాటలు సూచిస్తున్నాయి. ఇప్పుడు, తనే స్వంతముగా, ఒక అద్భుతమైన విషయాన్ని చెప్పదలుచుకున్నాడు. తన యొక్క ఎన్నో అద్భుతమైన విభూతులని తెలియచేసిన పిదప, ఆయన చెప్పిన దాన్నంతా కలిపినా తన యొక్క వైభవముల విస్తారాన్ని గణించలేమని అంటున్నాడు, ఎందుకంటే అనంతకోటి బ్రహ్మాండముల సృష్టి ని తన యొక్క చిన్న అంశ యందే కలిగి ఉన్నాడు, శ్రీ కృష్ణుడు.

తన యొక్క చిన్న అంశ ను ఇక్కడే ఎందుకు ఉదహరిస్తున్నాడు? కారణం ఏమిటంటే, అనంతమైన బ్రహ్మాండములు కలిగి ఉన్న మొత్తం భౌతిక సృష్టి, భగవంతుని సమస్త సృష్టిలో కేవలం 1/4వ వంతు మాత్రమే; మిగిలిన 3/4వ వంతు ఆధ్యాత్మిక దివ్యమైన సృష్టి.

పాదోఽస్య విశ్వ భూతాని త్రిపాదస్యామృతం దివి (పురుష సూక్తం, 3వ మంత్రం)

"భౌతిక శక్తి చే తయారుచేయబడిన ఈ యొక్క తాత్కాలికమైన జగత్తు పరమేశ్వరుని యొక్క ఒక్క భాగము మాత్రమే. మిగతా మూడు భాగాలు, జనన-మరణములకు అతీతమైన ఆయన యొక్క దివ్య ధామములు."

ఆసక్తికరంగా, శ్రీ కృష్ణుడు అర్జునుడి ముందే, ఈ లోకం యందే, ఉన్నాడు, అయినా సమస్త భౌతిక జగత్తు తన ఒక అంశలోనే ఉన్నది అంటున్నాడు. ఇది గణేశుడు మరియు శివుని కథ లాగా ఉంది. ఒకసారి, నారద మహర్షి శివునికి ఒక ప్రత్యేకమైన పండు ఇచ్చాడు. శంకర భగవానుని ఇద్దరు కుమారులైన, కార్తికేయుడు మరియు గణేశుడు ఇద్దరూ దానికోసం అడిగారు. తను వారిలో ఏ ఒక్కరికైనా ఇస్తే, రెండవవారు తమ తండ్రి పక్షపాతముగలవాడని అనుకుంటారని శంకరుడు తలచాడు. కాబట్టి శంకర భగవానుడు తన ఇద్దరు పిల్లలకి ఒక పోటీ ఏర్పాటు చేసాడు. ఎవరైతే ఈ బ్రహ్మాండమును ప్రదక్షిణ చేసి, తిరిగి తన దగ్గరికి మొదట వస్తారో వారికే ఈ పండు అని అన్నాడు.

ఇది విన్న కార్తికేయుడు వెంటనే బ్రహ్మాండమును ప్రదక్షిణ చేయటానికి బయలుదేరాడు. ఆయన చక్కటి దేహధారుడ్యం కలవాడు కావున దానిని ఉపయోగించుకోదలచాడు. ఈయనతో పోలిస్తే, గణేశుడు ఊబకాయుడు మరియు తన తమ్మునితో పోటీ పడటానికి సరితూగను అనుకున్నాడు. కాబట్టి, వినాయకుడు (గణేశుడు) తన బుద్ధి ద్వారా దీనిని సాధించాలనుకున్నాడు. శివపార్వతులు అక్కడే నిలబడి ఉన్నారు. గణేశుడు వారికి మూడుసార్లు ప్రదక్షిణ చేసి, "నాన్నగారూ, నేను చేసేసాను, దయచేసి ఇక ఆ పండు ఇవ్వండి" అన్నాడు, శివుడు అన్నాడు "కానీ, నువ్వు మాతోటి ఇక్కడే ఉన్నావు కదా, బ్రహ్మాండము చుట్టూ ఎలా తిరిగావు" అని. గణేశుడు అన్నాడు, "తండ్రి గారు, మీరే ఈశ్వరుడు, సమస్త బ్రహ్మాండము మీ యందే ఉన్నాయి. నేను మీకు ప్రదక్షిణ చేస్తే సమస్త బ్రహ్మాండమును చుట్టి వచ్చినట్టే." తన పుత్రుడు గణేశుడు చాలా తెలివైన వాడని శంకర భగవానుడు ఒప్పుకోవలసి వచ్చింది మరియు నిజంగానే గణేశుడు ఆ పోటిలో నెగ్గాడు.

ఎట్లయితే శివుడు ఒక ప్రదేశంలోనే నిల్చున్నా, ప్రపంచమంతా తనలోయందే కలిగి ఉన్నట్టు, అదే విధంగా, అనంతమైన భౌతిక బ్రహ్మాండములను కలిగిఉన్న సమస్త సృష్టి, తన యొక్క ఒక్క అంశ యందే కలిగిఉన్నట్టు శ్రీ కృష్ణుడు అర్జునుడుకి ప్రకటిస్తున్నాడు.

అర్జున ఉవాచ ।

translation_english: After hearing this supremely secret spiritual knowledge which You have graciously revealed to me, my delusion is now gone.
explanation_english: Pidapa Arjuna was overjoyed to hear the blessings of Sri Krishna and the wisdom of the Supreme Lord, and he also realized that his lust had been destroyed. He accepted that Lord Krishna was not just his dear friend, but that he was the Supreme Lord, the source of all the riches of the world. Now, he begins this chapter with a grateful acknowledgment of Krishna's favor by imparting invaluable spiritual knowledge.

translation_english: I have heard from you in great detail about the production and non-manifesting of all beings, O lotus-eyed one, I have also heard about your eternal greatness.
explanation_english:
Arjuna continues to extol the greatness of Lord Krishna, believing in the supreme status of Lord Krishna as the cause of creation and dissolution of the entire material world. Sri Krishna is addressed as Kamala-Patraksha, which means large, soft, beautiful and having eyes like a lotus flower with the qualities of sweetness and softness."

In this sloka Arjuna says, "I have heard from you, O Lord Krishna, your ever-lasting, great glories.  Though Thou art in all, Thou art above their faults (they say unto Thee). You are the Supreme Appointer and at the same time, You are akarta and you are not responsible for our karmas. Although You are the bestower of our karmic results, You are impartial and equal to all. You are the Omniscient and the Bestower of Karmic Fruits. That is why I believe that You are the worshiper of all beings.

explanation_english: Arjuna declares that he accepts the reality of Sri Krishna's divine personality as he says. Although Arjuna had complete faith in his material form, he longed to see the universal form of Lord Krishna with all its opulences. He wishes to see it with his own eyes.

explanation_english: Earlier in the sloka, Arjuna wanted to see the cosmic form of Lord Sarvesvara. Now asking His permission. "O Yogeshwara, I have conveyed my desire to You. If You think I deserve it, please show me Your cosmic form and show me Your Yoga-richness". Yoga is the science of uniting the living soul with the Supreme Soul. Yogis are those who practice this Shasta. Yogeshwar also means "Lord of all Yogis". As that Paramatma is what all Yogis should ultimately attain, Sri Krishna therefore becomes Yogeshwar. Earlier in verse 10.17 Arjuna addressed the Lord as "Yogi", meaning "Master of Yoga". But now, in view of the increased respect for Lord Krishna, he changed it to "Yogeshwara".

Although the form is the same, it has infinite personalities with innumerable distinctive colors and different shapes. Sri Krishna used the words 'satashotha sahasrasah' which means innumerable forms and in many distinctive forms.

Having seen Arjuna in his cosmic form, which is composed of infinite shapes and colors, Lord Krishna now sees Arjuna in that cosmic form, the devas and other wonders.
